fixes.explanation: Money. The text says the Pharisees were "…lovers of money…" Jesus had just said that no servant can serve two masters, God and money (Luke 16:13). Hearing that and scoffing anyway tells you where their hearts were.
I can see why you'd guess it, friend, but the text doesn't say that about them. It says they were "…lovers of money…" That's the word Luke picks, so that's the word we keep.
Good guess, friend. But the verse names something else. It says the Pharisees were "…lovers of money…" Luke doesn't mention the Sabbath in that line at all.
A smile would've made for a friendlier scene, friend. But the text says they "…were scoffing at Jesus." That's the word the verse uses, and it isn't a smile.

A single stroke of a pen. Jesus says, "…it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law." That's about the smallest mark you could make. Even that tiny mark won't drop out of the Law.

A raindrop is tiny, but it's not what Jesus names. He says, "…a single stroke of a pen…" That's a small mark in writing. He says it's easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for that to drop out of the Law.

To warn them. He says, "Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment." He's asking for his five brothers, friend. He wants them warned so they don't end up where he is.

The Prophets. Abraham says, "They have Moses and the Prophets; let your brothers listen to them." So the brothers already have something to listen to. That's Abraham's answer to the request to send Lazarus.
Priests are a fair guess, but Abraham doesn't name them. He says, "They have Moses and the Prophets; let your brothers listen to them." The name that goes with Moses is the Prophets.
Abraham doesn't name the elders, friend. He says, "They have Moses and the Prophets; let your brothers listen to them." The name that goes with Moses is the Prophets.
